decomposedResolution.note: D10 was decomposed into four plain-language choices (the first re-framing was rejected as unintelligible; re-framed jargon-free and re-posed). The original write trigger remains OPEN; the four surrounding choices are answered below.
decomposedResolution.ordering: turn-number-AND-date-clock-time: a note keeps its order within its conversation and records when it was written, so notes from different agents are comparable and contradictions can judge recency (a turn count alone orders one conversation only; graphify-knowledge and the memory-lane review agree; D9 needs it too).
decomposedResolution.location: live-graphify-plus-committed-recovery-copy: working memory in graphify's always-on store, plus a smaller committed copy sufficient to rebuild/recover, so memory travels with a fresh clone without committing the whole graph. Requires per-note writes on graphify (whole-graph replace only today) and a defined recovery-copy contract; a measured graphify set already exceeds the size limit.
decomposedResolution.rewind: keep-marked-no-longer-current: notes from rewound turns stay in history but ordinary searches ignore them unless discarded paths are requested; preserves explanation, never treats a rewound note as current; consistent with D12.
decomposedResolution.sharing: OWNER DIRECTION, ratification pending. Single unified graph per repo mutualizing common project history, with per-job compartmentalization kept as a capability and pruning/query to avoid saturating each agent. Both properties must hold: unified management AND per-job compartmentalization. Atomicity depends on graphify; cross-repo/workspace sharing will matter; a single prune/queryable graph per repo is a candidate while performance holds. NOT the owner's alone: h2a, harness and graphify (and graphify's principal) must agree. Aligns with graphify-knowledge: namespace carries workspace, host and role become node attributes.
